svg.text: Pull the two breadboards about 2 cm apart. The ESP32 bridges the gap.
Its TOP pins go in row j (the last row) of the UPPER board.
Its BOTTOM pins go in row a (the first row) of the LOWER board.
USB port on the LEFT, like in your photo.
Green holes = free holes joined to the pin in the SAME column.
Top pins: use rows f, g, h, i above them. Bottom pins: rows b, c, d, e below.
Yellow = an ESP32 pin pushed fully into the hole.
Why it failed before: the pins were in the OUTER rows, so the ESP32
covered every hole joined to them, and the wires went into other groups.
Each column of 5 holes (a-e or f-j) is joined. Rows a-e and f-j are NOT joined across the middle.
